briefdescription.para: Extracts the type name from the __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ macro.

detaileddescription.para: This function template parses the compiler-specific __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ macro to extract a concise type name for the template parameter T.

Rather than relying on fixed character offsets (which are fragile across compiler versions and namespace changes), the implementation searches for the marker that introduces the template argument in the function signature string:

listitem.para: Clang formats the signature as "... [T = <typename>]", so the type name lies between the first "[T = " and the last ']'. The marker is searched for as a whole, since the type name may itself contain brackets (e.g. int[3]).

GCC formats the signature as "... [with T = <typename>]" or, on some versions, "... [with T = <typename>; ...]", so the type name starts after the first "[with T = " and ends at the following ';' or, if there is none, at the last ']'.

detaileddescription.para: If the marker is not found, or the compiler is not supported (e.g. MSVC, which uses __FUNCSIG__ instead of __PRETTY_FUNCTION__), the function returns "unknown" rather than failing to compile, since the name is used only to improve the test output.
The expected layouts are verified at compile time by the static_assert checks that follow the definition.

The name is spelled as the compiler prints it, and is used to identify the expected exception type in the throws<E> failure messages. Only clang and GCC are supported; with other compilers the function returns "unknown".

parameterdescription.para: The type whose name is to be extracted.

simplesect.para: A std::string_view containing the extracted type name, or "unknown" if it cannot be determined.

briefdescription.para: Reflection utilities for the µTest++ testing framework.

detaileddescription.para: The reflection namespace provides facilities for obtaining source location information and type names at compile time, thereby supporting advanced reporting and diagnostics within the µTest++ framework.

It includes a local implementation of source_location for standard libraries that do not yet provide std::source_location, as well as utilities for extracting file names from paths and concise type names from the compiler-specific __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ macro.
